aspire: Make short videos that help independent creators notice one practical creative decision at a time without turning the series into generic productivity advice.

audience.who: Independent creators who want useful creative process notes in a calm, repeatable short-video format.
audience.current_state: They scroll quickly, but they stay when the video names a real creative tension without shouting at them.
needs: A repeatable ending that feels steady
audience.promise: Each episode gives one precise creative move the viewer can try today.

creative_intent: Plan the next short video while preserving the series format, pacing, hook style, sound rhythm, visual rhythm, and audience promise.
current_state: Best-known episode structure: 2-second quiet hook, 8-second problem naming, 30-second example, 12-second practical move, 5-second closing line over a still workspace shot.
what_changed: Reduced the opening from a dramatic hook to a quiet tension line.
Kept one practical move per episode instead of a list of tips.
Made the ending repeatable: a calm closing line plus a still shot.
canon: Each episode is about one creative decision, not a full tutorial.
The host never claims a guaranteed outcome.
The format uses voiceover, hands or workspace visuals, and minimal on-screen text.
The closing line should leave the viewer steadier, not pressured.

style.hook: A quiet tension line that names a problem without hype.
style.pacing: Fast enough for short video, but with small pauses after the hook and before the closing line.
style.sound_rhythm: Warm voiceover, low background texture, no aggressive beat drop.
style.visual_rhythm: Hands, notebook, screen detail, object close-up, then a still workspace closing shot.
style.structure: Hook, problem, example, practical move, closing line.

prefer: A closing line that feels earned

causal_memory: The previous video worked because the hook named a familiar tension in plain language instead of chasing shock.
The example section held attention because it showed a real workspace object while the voiceover explained one decision.
The slower closing shot made the episode feel trustworthy and different from generic productivity content.
Keeping one practical move protected the audience promise.
external_context: Platform context: short vertical video where the first seconds matter, but the series should not imitate viral-bait pacing.
Session context: the next AI may be asked to write script, shot list, or edit notes, but not to post or optimize analytics.
Audience has low patience for vague creator advice and exaggerated claims.
open_questions: Should the next episode focus on choosing a constraint, preserving voice, or ending a draft?
Should the visual object be a notebook page, a timeline edit, or a messy desk detail?
next_move: Draft the next episode outline using the best-known structure. Start with three quiet hook options, then choose one and build a 45 to 60 second script around one practical creative move.
stop_condition: Stop if asked to make unsafe claims or promise guaranteed creative results.
Stop if the episode turns into a generic viral advice format.
Stop if the series audience changes from independent creators to broad productivity content.
Stop if platform-specific claims are needed but not provided.
reanchor_condition: Re-anchor if the episode length changes beyond 45 to 60 seconds.
Re-anchor if the host style changes from calm voiceover to high-energy direct address.
Re-anchor if the series becomes a tutorial series, product launch, or trend reaction format.
Re-anchor if a new episode outperforms the current best-known structure for reasons the creator wants to preserve.
next_ai_should_not: Do not write a generic viral-bait hook.
Do not add fake urgency, fake metrics, or guaranteed outcomes.
Do not change the recurring format into a listicle or tutorial.
Do not overload the video with captions or too many tips.
Do not shift the audience promise away from one precise creative move.
handoff_prompt: Continue this short-video series using the attached Creator Continuity Record. Preserve the best-known episode structure: quiet 2-second hook, problem naming, concrete example, one practical move, and still workspace closing shot. Start with three quiet hook options and do not use viral-bait, fake urgency, unsafe claims, or analytics promises.
notes: This record supports scripts, shot lists, and edit notes. It is not an auto-posting or analytics workflow.
